## What is verified, and where

- **The numerical core** (`core/`, Rust compiled to WebAssembly) has a
  validation suite that `cargo test --release` runs on every push. Every
  claim in the text that rests on one of its tests carries a ✓ badge
  linking to the test.
- **The API documentation** of the core is published with the report at
  [api/](../api/qs_core/index.html); the ⟨name⟩ marks in the text link
  to the function that evaluates the equation next to them.
- **Citations** were verified against SAO/NASA ADS before they entered the
  bibliography; each entry keeps its bibcode.
- **The steady model** (Julia, `steady/`) is the reference implementation. The
  browser core is a port of it, and its tests compare against values exported
  from the Julia code (`steady/scripts/export_reference.jl`).
- **The TITAN port** (`julia/`) is verified against the original Fortran in three
  tiers (@sec-port-method); the record is `docs/PORTING_NOTES.md`. The TITAN figures
  replay stored run output; they are not recomputed in the browser.
- **Open items** are stated where they arise. The TITAN infall runs survive the accretion shock up to
  $3\,M_\odot\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$. Resolving the cooling layer behind the shock (adaptive grid, converged in the zone count
  to $\sim\!10^{-3}R$) the star settles within $1.4\times10^{-3}R$ and 50 K of the steady model; why it does not settle
  exactly there is open (@sec-infall-adaptive).

## Lineage

This book grew from working notes of 15–16 October 2026. The PDF version of the
steady-model notes is in `steady/paper/`; its tables predate a code revision and are superseded by this book
(@sec-branches). The TITAN 1.2 Fortran source (Gehmeyr &
Mihalas; UIUC licence, notice retained) is in `fortran/`.

## How to cite

The repository carries a `CITATION.cff`; GitHub shows it as "Cite this
repository". Until a DOI is minted, cite the repository and the commit above.

## Sharing a view of the laboratory

Every state of the laboratory is encoded in the address bar (the part after
`#`), so copying the URL shares the exact experiment; the *copy link* button
does this. Plots download as SVG or CSV from their toolbars.

## Annotating and discussing

Pages carry the Hypothesis sidebar: select any passage to annotate it.
Corrections are welcome as issues; every page has an *Edit this page* link.
